s1.syndrome_frame: Impacted tooth with associated radiographic lesion
salient_findings: Radiopaque lesion in the left mandibular anterior region
key_facts: 22-year-old woman
All permanent teeth erupted except third molars and lower left lateral incisor
Mild spacing between lower left central incisor and canine
Class II, Division 1 malocclusion
Crowding in maxillary anterior region
No history of prior dental extractions
Unerupted lower left lateral incisor with associated radiopaque lesion
Radiopaque lesion surrounded by thin radiolucent halo
Lesion obstructs eruption path of tooth

raw.syndrome_frame: Impacted tooth with associated radiographic lesion

shortlist.label: Compound odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Radiopaque lesion associated with unerupted tooth, consistent with odontoma

shortlist.label: Dentigerous cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Radiolucent halo surrounding radiopaque lesion, obstructing tooth eruption

shortlist.label: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Association with unerupted tooth and radiographic appearance

shortlist.label: Complex odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to compound odontoma, but with more complex structure

shortlist.label: Odontogenic keratocyst
shortlist.why_kept: Radiolucent lesion with potential to obstruct tooth eruption

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-defined radiopaque lesion surrounded by a thin radiolucent halo, associated with an unerupted tooth, is characteristic of an odontoma, and the compound type is more common in the anterior region and can prevent tooth eruption.

rejected.label: Dentigerous cyst
rejected.why: Typically associated with the crown of an unerupted tooth, not a distinct radiopaque mass

rejected.label: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: Usually presents as a radiolucent lesion, not radiopaque

rejected.label: Complex odontoma
rejected.why: More commonly found in the posterior region and does not typically have a distinct halo

rejected.label: Odontogenic keratocyst
rejected.why: Characterized by a radiolucent lesion, often with scalloped borders, not a radiopaque mass
